title: J. A. B. Rozier to Talleyrand, nos. 1 and 2, 6 Brumaire and 2 Frimaire an VII (27 Oct and 22 Nov 1798): the cipher letters of the Gibraltar packet sent to John Adams in March 1799

documents.shelfmark: MHS, Adams Family Papers, Adams Papers microfilm reel 393 (slip 100399, 'official dispatches, partly in cipher', 32 p., packet or Adams copies); the letters Pickering received in April 1799 (probably the originals), location not established; cover letter NARA RG 59, Letters Received, Jan-Jun 1799, Box 40, naId 55028996
documents.route: United States -> Paris (taken at sea; sent on by the US consul at Gibraltar, John Gavino)

plaintext.source: Rozier's own plain copies were shown to Pickering by 18 Jun 1799 (Pickering to Hamilton, PAH 23:199-200); their location is not recorded and no plaintext is in print. Pickering gives a two-sentence summary only.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary check-reading: Pickering to Hamilton, 18 Jun 1799 (Papers of Alexander Hamilton, ed. Syrett, vol. 23, 1976, pp. 199-200; Founders Online Hamilton/01-23-02-0200). Rozier 'exhibited his cypher' and plain copies; Pickering found 'in every passage examined, an exact correspondence' and summarised the content. No plaintext in print. Background PAH 23:12-13 n.1 (Founders Hamilton/01-23-02-0010).

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 628) and the rules; the AI agents searched the sources and a second agent re-read each one. No target-specific human intervention.
tools: Founders Online (read in a browser; scripts get a 202)

solution.what: PAH 23:12-13 n.1 (Founders Hamilton/01-23-02-0010): Cooper's 'List of papers received ... 27th March 1799' gives two Rozier letters to Talleyrand, 27 Oct and 22 Nov 1798 (with an extract to Hédouville, 20 Nov 1798), with the editors' 'Both letters are in code', and Gavino's dispatches; Cooper to Adams 28 Mar 1799 (Lovell 'despairs of being able to find a Key'); Pickering to Sands 31 May 1799 ('harmless').

PAH 23:199-200 (Founders Hamilton/01-23-02-0200): Pickering to Hamilton, 18 Jun 1799, checked the coded letters against Rozier's cypher and plain copies and summarised the content (parties, recent congressional elections, nothing hostile); note 1 quotes Pickering to Rozier, 12 Apr 1799 (letters nos. 1 and 2, 6 Brumaire and 2 Frimaire an VII, P.S. 3 Frimaire). Hamilton's letter of 13 Jun 1799 is 'Letter not found' (PAH 23:186). No plaintext printed.
Republican calendar: 1 Vendémiaire VII = 22 Sep 1798, so 6 Brumaire VII = 27 Oct 1798 and 2 Frimaire VII = 22 Nov 1798, Cooper's two dates; Pickering's nos. 1 and 2 are the two letters of the packet.
MHS slip file 100399 (Consul at Gibraltar to JA, ante 27 Mar 1799, 'official dispatches, partly in cipher', 32 p.) and 100403 (Cooper to JA, 28 Mar 1799): Adams Papers microfilm reel 393, not online.
NARA naId 55028996 (Adams to Pickering, 1 Apr 1799, RG 59 Letters Received, Box 40): no digital objects; scope note 'they have not been deciphered'; marked not available to researchers.
Three web searches (English and French) for an edition of the Rozier letters, a printed plaintext or a study of Rozier's cypher: none found. Short search only.

Second agent re-read every cited source: quotations confirmed; outcome narrowed from 'earlier solution found' to a contemporary check-reading with summary only; Gavino dispatches being plain is an inference; 'keep the copies from abroad' is ambiguous; Rozier to Pickering 3 Apr 1799 'not found' is our search result, not the editors'.

Review: the four Founders Online pages (Hamilton/01-23-02-0010, -0183, -0200; Adams/99-02-02-3399) re-read in a browser. Quotations confirmed; Adams's own letter has Lovell 'despairs of being able to make a key'; 'Both letters are in code' is the editors' sentence, not Cooper's; Gavino's letter of 13 Feb 1799 is cited as an autograph in the Adams Family Papers; whether Pickering received originals or copies is not stated. Republican-calendar dates recomputed.

outcome.method_basis: No image of either letter is online (MHS microfilm reel 393; NARA naId 55028996 without images), so no ciphertext was seen. The work is a pointer: the packet's contents identified and dated, and Pickering's contemporary check-reading cited exactly.
